review_notes:
I reviewed all 202 lines. The file builds `Realizer` terms, polynomial-time bounds and weight lemmas for list operations that Mathlib and Lean core already define. Every specification uses the existing operation directly: `List.dedup`, `List.orderedInsert`, `List.insertionSort`, `List.toFinset`, `Finset.sort` and list membership. So the file does not set up its own competing version of those concepts. `canonical_eq_sort` connects the computed form back to Mathlib's `Finset.sort`. That is integration with Mathlib, not duplication.

I checked the project for independent competing declarations. I grepped for `dedup`, `contains`, `orderedInsert`, `insertionSort`, `canonical`, `dedupStep`, `insertStep` and `weight_perm`. The matches with the same names are in unrelated namespaces and mean different things. Examples are `contains` on tries or balls, `dedup : List ℤ → …` with costs, and the many unrelated `canonical` definitions. No other `TreeTyped` realizer duplicates these.

The closest match is the local helper `dedupStep`, at line 25: `if x.1∈x.2 then x.2 else x.1::x.2`. It is essentially an uncurried `List.insert`. In Lean core (`Init/Data/List/Basic.lean`), `List.insert` is defined as `if l.contains a then l else a :: l`. However, core's version tests membership with `BEq`/`contains`, while `dedupStep` uses `DecidableEq` and `∈`; the two agree only when `BEq` is lawful. `dedupStep` also takes a pair, which is the shape the `fold` combinator needs. It is used only inside this file, by `dedupStepRealizer`, `dedup_fold` and `weight_dedupFold`. Switching to `List.insert` would mainly change proof details, and there is no duplicated API or repeated conversion to remove. Since the practical case for consolidating is unclear, I did not report it.

`insertStep` is an encoding-specific state transition with no counterpart in Mathlib. `weight_perm` is a theorem, so it falls outside this rubric.
